arxiv-2108-03356.title: HelpViz: Automatic Generation of Contextual Visual Mobile Tutorials from Text-Based Instructions Conference: The 34th Annual ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology; October 10–14, 2021; Virtual Event, USA The 34th Annual ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology (UIST
arxiv-2108-03356.creator: Mingyuan Zhong, Gang Li, Peggy Chi, Yang Li
arxiv-2108-03356.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Mingyuan Zhong, Gang Li, Peggy Chi, Yang Li. We present HelpViz, a tool for generating contextual visual mobile tutorials from text-based instructions that are abundant on the web. HelpViz transforms text instructions to graphical tutorials in batch, by extracting a sequence of actions from each text instruction through an instruction parsing model, and executing the extracted actions on a simulation infrastructure that manages an array of Android emulators.

arxiv-2201-07901.title: Extending the Lorentz Factor Range and Sensitivity of Transition Radiation with Compound Radiators
arxiv-2201-07901.creator: Samer T. Alnussirat & Michael L. Cherry
arxiv-2201-07901.description: Abstract Transition radiation detectors (TRDs) have been used to identify high-energy particles (in particular, to separate electrons from heavier particles) in accelerator experiments. In space, they have been used to identify cosmic-ray electrons and measure the energies of cosmic-ray nuclei.

arxiv-2203-09493.title: Modellieren mit Heraklit
arxiv-2203-09493.creator: Peter Fettke, Wolfgang Reisig
arxiv-2203-09493.description: Abstract Heraklit ist ein laufendes Forschungsprogramm und Entwicklungsprojekt mit dem Ziel der Schaffung einer Infrastruktur zur Modellierung großer, rechnerintegrierter Systeme. Wir diskutieren die zentralen Anforderungen an solche Modelle (Hierarchien, Nutzersicht, Überführung informaler in formale Ideen, schematische Modelle, gleichrangiger Umgang mit digitalisierten und personengebundenen Prozessen) und erläutern, wie Heraklit diese Anforderungen unterstützt.

arxiv-2303-07601.title: V2V4Real: A Real-world Large-scale Dataset for Vehicle-to-Vehicle Cooperative Perception
arxiv-2303-07601.creator: Runsheng Xu, Xin Xia, Jinlong Li, Hanzhao Li, Shuo Zhang, Zhengzhong Tu, Zonglin Meng, Hao Xiang, Xiaoyu Dong, Rui Song, Hongkai Yu, Bolei Zhou, Jiaqi Ma, University of California, Los Angeles Cleveland State University University of Texas at Austin, Northwestern University Technical University of M
arxiv-2303-07601.description: Abstract Modern perception systems of autonomous vehicles are known to be sensitive to occlusions and lack the capability of long perceiving range. It has been one of the key bottlenecks that prevents Level 5 autonomy. Recent research has demonstrated that the Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V) cooperative perception system has great potential to revolutionize the autonomous driving industry.

arxiv-2306-11593.title: Improving Image Captioning Descriptiveness by Ranking and LLM-based Fusion
arxiv-2306-11593.creator: Simone Bianco, Luigi Celona, Marco Donzella, Paolo Napoletano
arxiv-2306-11593.description: Abstract State-of-The-Art (SoTA) image captioning models often rely on the Microsoft COCO (MS-COCO) dataset for training. This dataset contains annotations provided by human annotators, who typically produce captions averaging around ten tokens. However, this constraint presents a challenge in effectively capturing complex scenes and conveying detailed information.

arxiv-2309-14553.title: Inverse non-linear problem of the long wave run-up on coast To appear in Journal of Ocean Engineering and Marine Energy
arxiv-2309-14553.creator: Alexei Rybkin, Efim Pelinovsky, Oleksandr Bobrovnikov, Noah Palmer
arxiv-2309-14553.description: Abstract The study of the process of catastrophic tsunami-type waves on the coast makes it possible to determine the destructive force of waves on the coast. In hydrodynamics, the one-dimensional theory of the run-up of non-linear waves on a flat slope has gained great popularity, within which rigorous analytical results have been obtained in the class of non-breaking waves.

arxiv-2310-01203.title: Escape from an Orbiting Pursuer with a Nonzero Capture Radius Thanks: This research was funded by Air Force Research Laboratory under FA8650-20-2-5853 and 21RQCOR084. Distribution Statement A: Approved for public release. Distribution is unlimited. Case number AFRL-2023-4713.
arxiv-2310-01203.creator: Braulio Mora, Alexander Von Moll, Isaac Weintraub, David W. Casbeer, Animesh Chakravarthy
arxiv-2310-01203.description: Abstract This paper explores a multi-agent containment problem, where a fast evader, modeled having constant speed and using constant heading, attempts to escape a circular containment region that is orbited by a slower pursuer with a nonzero capture radius. The pursuer is constrained to move along the edge of the containment region and seeks to capture the evader.

arxiv-2405-12466.title: Phases and dynamics of few fermionic impurities immersed in two-dimensional boson droplets
arxiv-2405-12466.creator: Jose Carlos Pelayo ∗, Thomás Fogarty, Thomas Busch, Simeon I. Mistakidis
arxiv-2405-12466.description: Abstract We unravel the ground state properties and emergent non-equilibrium dynamics of a mixture consisting of a few spin-polarized fermions embedded in a two-dimensional bosonic quantum droplet. For an increasingly attractive droplet-fermion interaction we find a transition from a spatially delocalized fermion configuration to a state where the fermions are highly localized and isolated.

arxiv-2411-18746.title: Inference Privacy: Properties and Mechanisms
arxiv-2411-18746.creator: Fengwei Tian Ravi Tandon
arxiv-2411-18746.description: Abstract Ensuring privacy during inference stage is crucial to prevent malicious third parties from reconstructing users’ private inputs from outputs of public models. Despite a large body of literature on privacy preserving learning (which ensures privacy of training data), there is no existing systematic framework to ensure the privacy of users’ data during inference.

arxiv-2511-14611.title: SecureSign: Bridging Security and UX in Mobile Web3 through Emulated EIP-6963 Sandboxing
arxiv-2511-14611.creator: Charles Cheng Ji, Brandon Kong
arxiv-2511-14611.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Charles Cheng Ji, Brandon Kong. Mobile Web3 faces catastrophic retention ( < 5 % <5\% ) yielding effective acquisition costs of $ 500 − $ 1,000 \$500-\$1,000 per retained user. Existing solutions force an impossible tradeoff: embedded wallets achieve moderate usability but suffer inherent click-jacking vulnerabilities; app wallets maintain security at the cost of 2 − 3 % 2-3\% retention due to download friction and context-switching penalties.

pmc-10541886.title: The role of Lactobacillus in inflammatory bowel disease: from actualities to prospects
pmc-10541886.creator: Congxin Li, Kaixin Peng, Siqi Xiao, Yuanyuan Long, Qin Yu
pmc-10541886.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Inflammatory Bowel Disease (IBD), a chronic nonspecific intestinal inflammatory disease, is comprised of Ulcerative Colitis (UC) and Crohn’s Disease (CD). IBD is closely related to a systemic inflammatory reaction and affects the progression of many intestinal and extraintestinal diseases. As one of the representative bacteria for probiotic-assisted therapy in IBD, multiple strains of Lactobacillus have been proven to alleviate intestinal damage and strengthen the intestinal immunological barrier, epithelial cell barrier, and mucus barrier.

pmc-11331756.title: SUMOylation at the crossroads of gut health: insights into physiology and pathology
pmc-11331756.creator: Xue-Ni Ma, Mu-Yang Li, Guo-Qing Qi, Li-Na Wei, De-Kui Zhang
pmc-11331756.description: SUMOylation, a post-translational modification involving the covalent attachment of small ubiquitin-like modifier (SUMO) proteins to target substrates, plays a pivotal role at the intersection of gut health and disease, influencing various aspects of intestinal physiology and pathology. This review provides a comprehensive examination of SUMOylation’s diverse roles within the gut microenvironment.

pmc-11519576.title: Adversarial robustness improvement for X-ray bone segmentation using synthetic data created from computed tomography scans
pmc-11519576.creator: Wai Yan Ryana Fok, Andreas Fieselmann, Christian Huemmer, Ramyar Biniazan, Marcel Beister, Bernhard Geiger, Steffen Kappler, Sylvia Saalfeld
pmc-11519576.description: Deep learning-based image analysis offers great potential in clinical practice. However, it faces mainly two challenges: scarcity of large-scale annotated clinical data for training and susceptibility to adversarial data in inference. As an example, an artificial intelligence (AI) system could check patient positioning, by segmenting and evaluating relative positions of anatomical structures in medical images.

pmc-12996093.title: Dual-functional sulfonated PEEK implants via graphene oxide–mediated BMP-2 gene delivery: enhanced osteogenic and antibacterial performance in vitro
pmc-12996093.creator: Yueying Pan, Bumairemu Yiminjiang, Adilai Abula, Refeina Tuerxun, Maihefuzi Aishan
pmc-12996093.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionPolyetheretherketone (PEEK) is a promising orthopedic implant material due to its bone-mimetic mechanical properties; however, its bioinert surface and susceptibility to bacterial colonization limit its clinical efficacy. Strategies to enhance osteointegration while providing antibacterial functionality are urgently needed.MethodsGraphene oxide (GO) was functionalized with polyethylene glycol (PEG) and complexed with a plasmid encoding bone morphogenetic protein-2 (pBMP-2) to form a GO-PEG/pBMP-2 complex. This complex was coated onto sulfonated PEEK (SPEEK) via freeze-drying, yielding SPEEK-(GO-PEG/pBMP-2) composites.

pmc-13384747.title: Quaternary Climatic Changes and Biogeographic Barriers Drove Codiversification in the Obligate Mutualism Between Camponotus laevigatus and Its Endosymbiont Blochmanniella
pmc-13384747.creator: Swapnil S Boyane, Garrett J Behrends, Joseph D Manthey
pmc-13384747.description: Codiversification often arises when hosts and their endosymbionts share a linked evolutionary history, exhibit vertical transmission, or share ecological and biogeographic processes. Most studies on the codiversification of carpenter ants (genus Camponotus) have focused on the co‐phylogeny of hosts and endosymbionts across multiple species; however, no studies have examined the intraspecific population‐level phylogeographic patterns of codiversification within Camponotus.

pmc-13559071.title: A taurine metabolism-related gene program defines clinical and biological features of neuroblastoma and yields an 8-gene candidate prognostic model
pmc-13559071.creator: Benfu Zhong, Yanan Zhang, Zhaosong Wang, Qiuping Dong, Xin Li, Yuren Xia
pmc-13559071.description: BackgroundTaurine metabolism-related transcriptional programs have not been systematically characterized in neuroblastoma. We aimed to investigate the clinical relevance and biological features of a taurine metabolism-related gene program in neuroblastoma and to determine whether this candidate space could yield a prognostically informative gene signature.MethodsA taurine-related gene program was quantified using single-sample gene set enrichment analysis in the discovery cohort.
